rv.q: They elevate “Cats,” and certainly make it work for a new moment where queens now sit on thrones unimaginable in 1981.

A revival of Cats, at least in theory, might well give you paws. After a then-record 18-year run on Broadway—with a tagline, “NOW AND FOREVER,” that began to sound a bit like a threat—Andrew Lloyd Webber's synthtastic 1980s musical finally hung up its leotards and yak-hair wigs in 2000.
For the first time in forever, the show actually feels like “Now.”

I should say at this point that, no, I haven’t turned into a fan of the show itself, the one you can see at your community theater or license for your high school. I don’t believe musicals should need whisker consultants. But as happens occasionally, the right idea can transform the wrong material.
Cats: The Jellicle Ball is queen (and kween) of this and all other nights.
It's the musical event of the summer and the most fun I've ever had at an Andrew Lloyd Webber show.
The hottest club in New York City right now is downtown Manhattan's Arts Center, home to a must-see musical revival you never knew you needed

In fact, the only thing that makes this "Cats" worth watching is the ballroom environment of high and low drag that has been dropped like a bottle of Pooph odor eliminator onto Lloyd Webber's litter box of a musical.
Those adjectives are also a perfect fit for the ballroom setting and make for a really fun night at the theatre.

Admittedly, even at the end of this lengthy extravaganza, you may still not really understand what a “jellicle cat” is, but you will be jealous of your friends and neighbors if they get to see this groundbreaking production and you don’t.
Imagine my surprise when Cats: The Jellicle Ball, the new adaptation of the material now at the Arts Center, turned out to be a plentiful source of dazzle, fun and joy.
